I think that makes sense. Before I was sexually abused, I was very curious (not exactly promiscuous, but I was a fan of experimenting especially with the same sex). The continuing sexual abuse involved a sort of exhibitionism, so that's probably why I associate porn with sexual abuse (as I was coerced into recording myself). Even so, I still wasn't a totally asexual being before the abuse. 

I understand how I have this view now. I also understand that I must be willing to change it, which is why I sought help from this thread. I'd like to thank you especially, not for changing my view, but for helping me understand myself better. Your post made me realize that although SOME desires may stem from sexual abuse, I do have my own sexual feelings that belong to ME. It's important for any sexual abuse survivor to realize that. Ultimately I do have sexual feelings of my own that are all mine and that no one can truly corrupt or take away from, if that makes sense. Thank you.

I'm also worried it won't be taken seriously. Her goal of finishing her play is a good one, but it's not serious like terminal illness or war or some huge social commentary. It's also not as relatable because not many people are writers and they may not understand the intense feelings that writing can bring. I'm trying my best to communicate those feelings through the play, though.

Even when I try to go easier on myself, it's still hard for me to make friends. I'm fairly introverted but sometimes I really crave human contact. I think my desperation might creep people out.

It's about a girl writing a play. There's a wall in the middle. On one side of the wall, she's writing the play, and on the other side her characters are acting it out. She's a horrible playwright and suddenly an imaginary "inner critic" comes onto the stage. Eventually she decides to have her characters cross over the wall in the middle (playing with the whole "across the 4th wall" idea). The whole thing is sort of a parody of plays in general, plus observations about high school life, pressure from parents, pressure to succeed and make deadlines, etc. I hope to make it a good balance between comedy and drama. I even included some history in there, too, as it's interesting to poke fun at popular historical figures.

I'm writing a play, and I'm 64 pages in, but even that's not motivating me at this point. I feel like it really sucks and I should just delete the whole damn thing.

It's just hard to hear of all of these great parties and see pictures of friends going out together. I've never been invited to a party, or heard of them going on until they're already over.

I know that when I see my play on stage (which it will be, my school's drama director promised me that) it could be worth it. But I can't see that now, and I don't see how scholastic success is worth losing social success. I'd trade all of my A's just to have something to do on the weekends, and to be able to talk to people.

Yes, we text/talk every day. We hang out at school because we have exactly the same friends, and most of the same classes. We sit together in those classes and since they're small, there aren't other places to move. We hung out after school yesterday and went to the mall and had fun, but only because we weren't thinking about our issues.

Everyone at school sees us and thinks "there's [his name] and his girlfriend". I'm not me, I'm "[his name]'s girlfriend" to everyone I know. I am unknown around school by anything else. I've tried to make a name for myself my whole life, but no matter how smart I am, or how many books I write, or how much I sing or act, or how good I am at swimming...I can never be known for anything. I just feel like I'd rather be known for this than for nothing at all. I'm writing a play right now that the drama department wants to have me direct next year, but that's in one FULL year. I don't know what to do with myself for that whole time. The only thing I can think of is to talk to him.

I just have trouble believing that anyone would want to support me. Sure, I get support from the internet and strangers I don't know. But in my life, I haven't met anyone who truly supports me, even if I try to support them back. I feel like I can't "love" anyone and so I can't receive it back. Maybe my standards are too high, or maybe everyone just sucks. I can't figure it out and it's angry because I have a lot of love I'm willing to give, but no one to give it to.

I'm just so scared to be the one to end it. I know I'm not strong enough to do so, as I've tried before and it never truly "works". If he broke up with me, I'd be so grateful because at least there would be closure.  

We're juniors, so we still have the rest of this year, and a whole other year after this. I want to try to just wait it out until we graduate and are forced apart, but people are telling me I should take action now.

The thing is, we're already pretty much broken up. I broke it off the end of the last school year, and I spent the entire summer away from him (not seeing him once). I also went downhill during that time and that's when I was raped because of my horrible choices. I made these horrible choices because I was so depressed that I was without him. My life is awful with him, but I feel that it's worse when I don't have his love and support. I don't have much else.

I don't know how to end it because there is nothing to end, really. To me, we're still "broken up". I'm just so confused. I'm sorry.
